utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Loku.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your evidence will now continue. I remind you that the solemn declaration to tell the truth which you gave at the beginning of your evidence continues to apply to that evidence today. Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Loku. Yesterday, at the end of the day, we were looking at some photographs of a house for which you said you couldn't recognise as being one of the houses in the village of Kotlina. I am about to show you some other photographs, and I would kindly ask you to try and carry out the same exercise to be -- to see whether you are able to recognise anything. Could we please show 3D74 to the witness, page 6. To make it easier, perhaps the usher could also give the hard copy to the witness so that he could get his bearing more easily. I still don't see this in e-court. 3D74, page 6 of the document. Could you please put on the version in Serbian since the photographs are in that version. Your Honour, could I nevertheless try and move on with the witness without waiting for e-court? The witness has hard copies, and depending on his answer, we'll see whether I can continue after that, and in the meantime hopefully we'll get the picture. Thank you. Mr. Loku, the pages you were given from the document, this being pages 6, 7, 8, and 9 of Exhibit 3D74, I'll ask you this way: On the photographs in front of you, allegedly we can see two pits on some of the photographs, and those are allegedly the two pits you mentioned, as well as the bodies of some people who were found dead there. I think this is page 6 of this document. If you look at the third photograph from the top, or, rather, the photograph at the bottom of the page, you can see a large hole, a pit. Does this hole correspond to what you have in mind when you spoke about the two pits or the wells, depending on whichever term we wish to use?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the photo, you can see that there is a hole, a pit, but it didn't resemble those that are in the village at the mountain, because here I can see only the pit, or pits. I see some stairs. The photos seem rather old. I don't know what kind of photos these are. They are not clear, and they do not resemble the holes I mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe you know what those pits look like. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the holes in the village, what they looked like, what they were like before. The picture I see here at number 9 seems that there is water at the bottom of the hole. The holes I mentioned were dry, because they were dug by a villager who was searching for water, but he failed to find any water. On the basis of this photo, it's not like the one I mentioned because the place where the holes were is a mountainous area full of stones. You can see stones amid the earth, whereas these pits you are showing me seem smooth. They do not resemble the ones in our village.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And you know that because you had previously went -- gone to those pits. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't go there before that incident, but afterwards I went there, and I can say that there are stones. Wherever you can dig for water, you can run into stones.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Loku, is it your testimony now that before the event you never went up to those pits which were but 200 metres away from your school?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said this, yes. And I'm telling you there was no reason for me to go there. It was that villager who was looking for water who dug that place. I didn't have any reasons to go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did I understand your statement and your particulars well if I concluded that you have been born and raised and that you spent most of your life in the village of Kotlina, apart from the few recent years in your life?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I was born and brought up in the village of Kotline.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And you are testifying here today that up until after the event you never went up to the pits. Am I reading your testimony correctly? If this is so indeed, we can move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That question has been asked and answered. Please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show page 1 of the document to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Loku, from the place where you were, could you see the on-site investigation team of the Ministry of the Interior and the court of Urosevac who were there carrying out the investigation and taking photographs of certain spots in the village of Kotlina?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the place I was from which I observed the event of the 24th of March, I didn't see any other persons than those dressed in military and police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Loku, you couldn't recognise the house which is a part of the file. You are claiming that the pits on these photographs do not correspond to the pits which were -- which are just above your village. I presume the captions under the photographs that are in front you on pages 6, 7, and 8 also do not reflect the situation as you see it. Am I right in concluding that?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that these holes you are showing me are the ones that were in Kotline.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: But you were quite positive when you said that the house shown on the photograph shown to you yesterday was not a house from your village, and you also said that the weapons and the equipment that had been found -- or, rather, that it isn't possible that this was in your village. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already told you even yesterday that no armaments were found in any place in my village and that the houses showed me yesterday doesn't belong to my village. I explained this to you yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And this all tallies with your statement where on page 0081733 you stated, and I quote: "I know that not a single man was armed or a member of the KLA." Is this still your testimony?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is my testimony, that there wasn't a single KLA soldier in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Loku, are you in a dispute or a feud or in any other sort of conflict with a person from your village who was a member of the KLA, and his name was Xhezair Bela?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This name is not familiar to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Loku, were you able to observe that some wounded -- members of the KLA were wounded in your -- were treated in your school? There were two members of the KLA in question --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters apologise. We were unable to catch the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: -- and they were treated by a physician there.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I will repeat the names for the transcript. These are the wounded members of the KLA: Isa Medin [phoen] and Hasim Livareka [phoen] from the village of Bob, and physicians Fatmir Vila from Djeneral Jankovic, and Natal Sulejmani [phoen] from the village of Gorac. And I believe we have already received your answer.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time for me I hear these names. I don't know of any doctor by the name that you mentioned. These are names which I don't know. I never knew them. I never saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And in your school there were no members of the KLA who had been wounded and were treated at the school; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were only students in the school, but no soldier, or wounded soldiers as you are putting it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did you know that in your village there was a sub-unit of the KLA commanded by Selim Kuci, and his deputy was Limaj Kuci?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: All this, Mr. Loku, corresponds to what you testified about in the Milosevic trial when at page 2004 you state: "[In English] I don't remember to have seen any KLA members there. I'm saying that there wasn't any KLA members there." [Interpretation] Is that correct, Mr. Loku?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said is correct; namely, that there were no members of the KLA in my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Loku, your village is a small one. It had some 450 or 500 inhabitants out of which 100 were male, and you basically knew all of its inhabitants; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew each and every one of the persons who lived in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm just -- I'm not sure if the witness accepted that 100 of the people in his village were male. Just a matter for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you can take that up with him in re-examination. Carry on, please, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just to provide information to the learned friend, this is the Milosevic trial, page 1944. This is where I found the figure of 100 adult men.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Since we are discussing the Milosevic trial, on page 2005, you stated: "[In English] [Previous translation continues] ... and no confrontations between them and the Serb forces." [Interpretation] Also, at the same trial at page 2017, you said: "[In English] [Previous translation continues] ... in our village, and whoever wished to join KLA ranks, he might do so because KLA troops were in the mountains." [Interpretation] This is what you still stand by. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I stand by what I said at that time, because this is how the situation was like in the village. There wasn't a single KLA unit operating there. And those young people who wished to join its ranks might do so through various forms and ways. It is known that the KLA operated in various areas of Kacanik municipality, but not in my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Precisely so, Mr. Loku. And you stated that you know that not a single man carried arms or was a member of the KLA. And this is what you said in the statement and on page 00813733. You've confirmed this to me a moment ago. Hence, I want to ask you the following: Yesterday my learned friend Mr. Stamp mentioned a certain cemetery or a graveyard where a part of the inhabitants of your village were buried. That cemetery is in Kacanik. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, Mr. Loku, this is not a municipal or city graveyard of Kacanik. It is actually outside the settlement. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The cemetery is outside the village, but it is in the context of the Kacanik municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Correct. And it is at the crossroads of the roads for the villages of Stagovo and on the other side the village of Strpce; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And this is the road which you regularly take when you go from your house in Urosevac to your village. Am I correct? Or if you go towards Kacanik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In case -- in case --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- you're in any doubt about it, Mr. Visnjic, we have clearly in mind that some of the bodies were buried in a cemetery known as either a heroes' or a martyrs' cemetery of the KLA. Now, do you need any more evidence on this point? Or do you want to undermine what you've got?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, two things. First -- and I was about to start with that set of questions and I wish to be able to corroborate that with some additional evidence. Could we please show 3D71 to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Why do you -- why do you need to corroborate it? If you have a witness here who adamantly maintains there was no KLA activity in his village but nevertheless accepts that people who were killed in this incident were buried in the cemetery, don't you have the foundation of the argument you may wish to present later, or are you going to get more from the questions you intend to ask? Because if you're not confident of getting more, I suggest you move to something that's going to be more productive.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can freely state this: Apart from being able to corroborate that some people whose bodies were buried and who had been killed in that event on the 24th of March, that they were indeed buried in that cemetery, but there were some other inhabitants of his village who were members of the KLA buried in the same cemetery. This is what I wanted to -- the witness to confirm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. I accept that that is additional material, so please carry on. But you'll understand my concern that we did seem to be spending the best part of 25 minutes so far going nowhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show 3D81 to the witness, page 5. We don't have any translations since these are only photographs. 72. I'm sorry. 3D72. Page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Loku, this is Adnan Loku. This is the person you said was killed on the 24th, right? Page 6, please.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Loku, this is Neshat Rexha. This is a person you said that had come to visit his uncles in Kotlina, right? Also killed on the 24th of March.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was killed on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Page 7, please. Abush Loku. This person was also killed on the 24th. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you are not right. Abush Loku is a martyr killed in Koshare. He is from Kotline village, but he was killed somewhere else during the fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Ibush Loku is the name the person who was killed, right? So the name is similar except for the first letter?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Ibush, but this is not Ibush. This is Abush.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Page 8. Xhezair Bela is not an inhabitant of your village, right? So page 9, please.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Xhemajl Kuci.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is. He is -- he is an inhabitant of Kotline village.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: When was he killed? He was not killed on the 24th.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was killed on the 24th together with the other young men.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Photograph number 3, please, page 3. Mahi Loku.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Was he killed on the 24th?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was also killed on the 24th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: But he was not on that list that you read out to us yesterday.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only if his photograph was not there. Otherwise, he should be on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Photograph number 4. Sabri Loku.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was also killed on the 24th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And photograph number 7. Photograph number 7. Danush Loku.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No Danush Loku.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Danush Kuci?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Danush Kuci, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: He was a KLA soldier, too, right?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was not a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: All right. How many KLA soldiers were buried in this cemetery on the Urosevac-Kacanik road? People from your village, that is.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't count each and every one of them. I don't know, as I said earlier, how many were buried, reburied here in this cemetery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When did Danush Kuci die?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Danush Kuci, father's name Idriz, he was killed on the 24th of March in Kotline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: His name -- well, there is an Idriz Kuci on the schedule.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Idriz is Danush's father. He was killed on the same day as well. He was about 60 years old.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So that means that Danush does not appear on the schedule. And there may be an earlier name that does not appear on the schedule. You no, what -- just a moment. Mr. Visnjic, what may have been established here is it that schedule doesn't include everybody who was actually killed on the 24th, which expands the number of people that may have been killed on the 24th. No doubt the Prosecution will investigate that. I don't think we've established that there's anyone, according to this witness's evidence, so far in the cemetery from Kotlina who got there as the result of a death on a different day. So can we move to something that is productive now?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think that was the one from Kosare that was --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is one more, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: He gave his explanation that he was active in a different place.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I've been trying to find out from the witness how many persons were buried, because as you can see, these pictures were taken from quite a distance, and I do not have the possibility of having pictures taken of all the tombstones. And this is what I'm trying to get from the witness, the number of persons buried in the cemetery. He is not in a position to tell me. He doesn't know, as he said just now. I can move on to my next topic but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Loku, before I move on to my next topic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There must be way of getting photographs taken of all the tombstones, if that's what you want. Why can't that just be done?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You want me to tell you now or when the witness leaves? It would be better to leave it for later. I will have a comment regarding these photographs anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Loku, let me ask you now yet again. Do you still stand by this part of your statement that says, "I know that not a single man was a member of the KLA in my village"? That's what I'm asking you now.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated it earlier, and I stand by it now, that in my village on the day when this massacre was committed and these people were killed, there was not a single KLA member.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And you have no explanation why these persons were then buried in the KLA cemetery?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: My explanation is as follows: These persons that were buried in the martyrs' cemetery, they contributed to the national cause before the 24th of March. So the council that organised their reburial saw it necessary to bury them in the martyrs' cemetery. So these 27 men from the village that were killed on the 24th and two on the 9th, they would have been all proclaimed martyrs if they were killed in fighting, in combat with the Serbian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: No, Mr. Loku. They were not proclaimed martyrs because their pictures were taken in uniforms, and right next to them there is a coat of arms and a sign of the KLA. That is what I'm putting to you, Mr. Loku. And I'm also putting to you that when you stated in your statement and what you said at the Milosevic case under oath is not correct. That is what I'm putting to you. That is my assertion, Mr. Loku. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question. If you can repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Loku, I'm putting to you the following: What you said in your statement -- just a moment, please. 00813733, and what you said at the Milosevic case on page 2004 and 2005 and 2017, namely that there were no members of the KLA in your village, that all of that is not correct, and I claim that you are not telling the truth. And I claim that these photographs prove it.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you the truth, that in my village there were no uniformed persons, rather, persons carrying -- wearing KLA uniforms or persons who offered resistance to the Serbian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: No, no, Mr. Loku. I'm asking you whether there were any KLA members in your village. Now, that's your assertion.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already told you that there were no members. And these persons that you are mentioning as members of the KLA, they were not soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So what were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were villagers, ordinary citizens from the village. Three of them were teachers in my school, and they had contributed for years with the national cause in different ways in the education sphere and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So they're buried there because they were teachers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was one of the reasons. They were teachers. They worked on the national cause. And the council who carried out the reburial, they should know better why they chose to bury them in this martyrs' cemetery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We understand that, but we don't have them here. We have you here, and we'd like to know what the explanation is for them being in the martyrs' cemetery. One of them that you've identified as in the cemetery was only 16. Now, why was he buried in the martyrs' cemetery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 16-year-old was not buried in the martyrs' cemetery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Neshat Rexha was not buried there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Neshat Rexha was buried there, but he is not from Kotlina village, and I don't know his date of birth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But you -- he is the one who was visiting; is that correct? He was the one who was visiting his uncle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct. He was at his uncle's place when he was killed on that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Naser Loku, was he buried there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Naser Loku? Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: He was 17.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand. 70 years old?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Seventeen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 7-0 was the age of Zimer Loku.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no. He was 17 years of age.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Seventeen years old were two persons who had the name Naser. The 17-year-old was buried in the village cemetery. We have Naser Fazli Loku, Fazli being father's name; and Naser Rexhep Loku, Rexhep being the father's name. So two persons with the first name Naser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, can you help us by being any more specific about what service they would have done -- those who were buried there would have done for the KLA to deserve the title "martyrs"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot provide any explanation about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If you had been killed that day would you expect to have been buried in that cemetery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Loku, in your statement, you said that you had two plans for the evacuation of the village; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not two plans but two directions, two paths that could take us outside the village, because we were not planning to leave the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: So what it says in your statement, paragraph 4 on page 1 -- let me just have a look at the English version. In the English version as well. It says: "We had two plans for the evacuation of the village." That is incorrect. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The word "plan" has a different meaning, because we didn't have any plans, but when it happened, there were two directions. That was a plan that was made accordingly to what had happened, not from before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's the reference to that, Mr. Visnjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the statement in English, page 2, paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You don't have the transcript reference from yesterday? Because my recollection is that it was two ways --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I have a different indication. The wording used yesterday was somewhat different. That's why I'm asking the witness. Yesterday he said -- I just have the quotation, I don't have the reference. "[In English] [Previous translation continues] ... they choose the place where they would go to." [Interpretation] That is what he stated yesterday. In the statement, it says that there was a plan, but I'm going to accept the explanation provided by the witness just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Now, in your statement you say you were with your relative, Heset Loku. That is page --

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be Heset, H-e-s-e-t.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Heset Loku. The page is 00813732. Now I'm asking you the following: Was Heset a member of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until the 24th of March, Heset wasn't a KLA member. We went together to Macedonia, but after some time he returned to Kosova and became a KLA member.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: So binoculars is part of his regular equipment like -- as a regular civilian, that is?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were hunting binoculars that we took with us by accident from Stimlje.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Right. Now, I would ask for 3D88 to be prepared. And before that I'm going to ask you the following: In your statement you said that you were about 400 metres away from those two holes or pits that were later blown up. Yesterday, during the course of your testimony, you said the distance involved was 500 to 600 metres. Is there any special reason for that change or was it, well, just like that, just a question of estimate, your own estimate?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm wondering if my friend can assist us with the references for those sections cited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't think we need these. I've certainly got a clear recollection that that was the evidence yesterday. Please just move on, Mr. Visnjic. If there's someone assisting you who can help, then so it be, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Loku, now we have a photograph here of your village, which was taken from the road leading from Kacanik to your village. I'm asking you the following: From this view-point, were you further away from this position or can you tell me approximately in terms of distance?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this view-point, I was on the left side of this photograph. You cannot see the place where I was on the photograph. I stated it yesterday that I was on the opposite side of the village. The village is in a shape of a semicircle, and we are now talking about a distance in terms of --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: So you were even further away from this it place, right?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not further from this place. Closer, but from a different angle, because you cannot see the holes from this point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Well, you cannot see them because they're on the right, and if you were further away, you could have only been on the left. That's why I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was on the left but closer to the houses in the village, and the holes were in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Were you at a position that was lower than this place in terms of altitude?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not lower than this place. It could have been even a couple of metres higher in terms of altitude. And the place, as I said, where I was, if compared to this place on the photograph, was higher for couple of metres, in terms of altitude.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Could the witness now please be shown Defence Exhibit -- or, rather, the same document but page 9. Mr. Loku, is this the hill where the pits are, where the holes are?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the hill where the holes are. Above the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And this black dot in the middle of the hill, the computer image is not very focused, but would that be where the pits are?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Could the witness now please be shown the following photographs: 3. You see, Mr. Loku, it's the same place but just a bit enlarged. Then photograph number 5.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And photograph number 7.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Loku, does this correspond to what you saw on the 24th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were the holes and what I saw on the 24th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: You said that you saw this with the naked eye and that you didn't have to use any binoculars, or is this just my understanding of your statement?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had the binoculars. We were watching through binoculars but with the naked eye as well. And we didn't need the binoculars that much. But on the 24th of March when the incident happened there wasn't such vegetation. You could see clearly everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: How come you know when this picture was taken, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I see on this photograph, the photograph must have been taken in mid-August, because there the -- the vegetation starts in early May. So there couldn't be that much vegetation on the 24th of March when it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Loku, now you've got a new problem, because these photographs were taken on the 24th of May, when you said that there is no vegetation. The 24th of May. Yes, that's what I said. The transcript is right. Now, I'm going to ask you about the following --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The witness did not say there was no vegetation on the 24th of May. He said that the vegetation starts at the beginning of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then, Your Honour, it seems that it blossoms pretty fast from the beginning of May until the 24th of May. But let's look at a few other photographs. 22, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Loku, you see, this photograph was taken above both wells, because at any other place other than this it was impossible to see anything in terms of this area in fronts of you because of all the greenery around it. Now I'm asking you the following -- or, rather, as for this place where the wells are, is that where you can approximately see this road from which we took the previous photographs? Would that seem right to what you know in terms of the location of the holes?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm repeating it. I told you that this photo is taken during a blossom, and when there is vegetation, you can't see things. So I cannot give any other explanation for this picture because I don't -- you can't see anything there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I suspect you'll have at least two winters in which to take the appropriate photographs, Mr. Visnjic, and let us see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in view of the latest developments, I'm afraid that you're right, but we'll see how things go.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I'll somehow you a few more photographs, so I'd kindly ask you to identify them for me. Photograph number 15, please. Mr. Loku, does this photograph correspond to the foot of the hill? It was taken somewhere near the clinic, the infirmary. As far as you're concerned, would this seem right? Or perhaps we can move on to the next one because this one is not very clear. There's nothing specific here. Let's see photograph number 16, please. This is yet another photograph from the top, rather, above the holes that shows roughly the right-hand side where you said you were. Mr. Loku, as you can see, in the middle of the photograph we see a bit of the roof-tops. Is this roughly where you were?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would kindly ask you to prevent such questions being asked of me using such photos with vegetation, because when there is vegetation, it's difficult to discern something. If they wanted to put photos to me, they should have shown me photos of that time, of the 24th of March of other years to see what one can see on that day of the year. Do not show me such colour -- green-coloured photos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Loku, I can assure you it's not a simple exercise to get the photographs that may be necessary for the preparation of a case like this, and while I understand the point you're making, it's your duty to do your best to answer the question. Now, if you can't answer it because it's impossible, you can just say that. But it's not for us to stop the questions being asked in this these circumstances. It's for you simply to say that you can't be of assistance when faced with a photograph of this nature, which is what I take to be your answer to that question. And no doubt Mr. Visnjic will now move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we show for number 19 to the witness, please. This is the same one. Let us move on. Number 20, please. No. No. Then photograph number 18, and I will conclude with this. No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let me check first. I have no more questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I want to begin with a request that we go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In broad terms, would you please tell me why?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I can't in the presence of the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we can have the witness leave the courtroom while you want to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Then I'd be happy to do it if the witness is not in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Loku, could you withdraw just very briefly from the court and you'll be back in a couple of minutes. The usher will show you where to go just for the moment while I hear a submission about the law.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the testimony of the witness yesterday, beginning at page 3167 of the transcript, Mr. Stamp was asking him about the place where these people were buried. He said that most of them were buried in the schoolyard. He was asked where the others were buried and he said they were buried in other place. He was asked what the other place was, and he said: "Some were buried at Kacanik cemetery." He was asked if that was associated with any organisation. He said: "This I don't know." Now, we know now that was not a true answer. He was asked: "Did you hear anything about any organisation that the Kacanik cemetery might have been associated with?" His answer was no. And we know now that that was not a true answer. And then finally Mr. Stamp had to ask a leading question because he knew that this was in the statement the man had given: "Do you know whether or not any of these persons who are buried in a cemetery that is associated with the KLA?" And after a few more questions he finally was able to drag that out of him and get him to agree that that was the case. I want to go into closed session because I have a theory that I want to test with the witness, and I may not get anywhere with it and I may. But what I think was going on yesterday and what seems kind of obvious to me what was going on yesterday was that it was a public hearing, and he was afraid for what would happen to him when he went back home if he said there were KLA in his village, if he said that some of these people that were killed there were KLA, and he was very reluctant to say that until it was absolutely forced out of him so that he can defend himself when he goes home. I'd like to go into closed session and just ask him if that's the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, do you want to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No. No, Your Honour. I thought the explanations could have been broader if they were security issues, but I have no comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Just give us a moment to consider the position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We'll grant this application on the broad basis that it's in the interests of the security of the witness. It will simply be private session that's required, I take it. We won't need to bring down the blinds.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I keep getting those mixed up, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So when the witness comes back, we will go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like you to explain to him that we're in private session and what that means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I will explain that to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So he's completely assured that nothing's going outside this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, it may be that your objective could be inadvertently defeated if the reason wasn't in fact redacted from the public transcript. The basic reason that I've given need not be redacted but the explanation probably should.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So what I think we'll do is in the circumstances redact the whole of the section from your submission, and then I will repeat the reason in a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Your Honour for realising that. I should have realised it myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So I'm grateful to the Registrar for making that suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thanks to the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in private session at the moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well -- okay. Mr. Loku, I have granted the application to hear the next part of your evidence in what's called private session. That means that all that transpires here is in private. Nothing can been heard by anyone outside. Nothing can be reported about what is said by you in answer to the questions that are about to be asked. So we are essentially behind closed doors, with one slight modification that what's going on can be seen from the outside, but that simply indicates that the public can see that a court is in session. They can't hear anything that goes on in that session. So these are the circumstances under which the next part of the evidence will be heard. Mr. Ackerman will now start his cross-examination. Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, could you also assure him that nothing that's said here will be later furnished to the public in any way. It remains private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, indeed, I think I've already said that nothing can be reported either now or later about what is actually said here. So carry on now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Loku, my name is John Ackerman. I represent General Pavkovic in this case, and I have a few questions I want to ask you, and I want to start with some testimony you gave yesterday. Actually, I want to start a little bit ahead of that. You -- when you came here, you had a conversation with some representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor, Irina Dragulev, Associate Legal Officer, and that was on the 5th of September where you made some corrections and provided some additional information regarding your testimony, your story. Do you recall doing that?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And in that supplemental information sheet --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, that has now been put in the system as Exhibit 4D16.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: In that supplemental information sheet in paragraph 6 you made this revelation: "Half the victims were buried on a cemetery of the schoolyard. The other half were declared KLA heroes and buried on the KLA cemetery." Now, according to this representative of the Prosecutor's office, that's what you told them that day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way I understand your question is I stated that I said stated approximately a half. I didn't count the number of those buried in the schoolyard and those buried at the martyrs' cemetery. But I didn't say they were proclaimed heroes. They are just victims of the war, martyrs of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So when Ms. Dragulev or whoever else might have been assisting her wrote in this supplemental information sheet that you had said that, that was misinformation. She was wrong. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe there has been a mistake during the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. Now, yesterday you certainly mentioned to her, no question about that, that some of these people were buried in the KLA cemetery. No question about what you said there, is there?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it yesterday too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm asking about September 5th. You said it then, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said it on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, yesterday Mr. Stamp was asking you about this, about where these people were buried, and you said: "Most of them were buried in the schoolyard." And then he asked you: "Where were the others buried? You said yes. Then he said: "Where were the others buried, do you know?" And then you said: "The others were buried in another place. In the cemetery." Mr. Stamp then asks you: "What was that other place? Can you describe it for me, please?" You said: "Yes, I can. Some of them were buried at Kacanik cemetery. Those who are not buried at the schoolyard are buried at Kacanik cemetery." Then Mr. Stamp said this, having read what you told

utterances.speaker: MS. DRAGULEV
utterances.text: "Now, the Kacanik cemetery, was it associated or did it belong to any organisation?" And you told us, under oath: "This I don't know." And then Mr. Stamp said: "Well, did you hear anything about any organisation that the Kacanik cemetery might have been associated with?" And again you told us no. Now, those two answers were clearly not true. And what I want to ask you is this: Did you give those answers because you were afraid that people outside this courtroom might take some kind of action against you when you went home if you admitted that there were KLA in your village? Did you give the answers this way because of fear of what would happen to you when you got home? Understand no one can hear this exchange, this is very private. So you can be honest.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday, and I will repeat today, as far as I am concerned, you can go into public session, because the way I understood the question of me was associated with some other organisation. I didn't understand that it was -- it meant the cemetery, the martyrs' cemetery. This other organisation, for me, was not clear. That's why I said what I said. I am not afraid of anyone. I have not been threatened by anyone, and I didn't consult the opinion of anyone before coming here. I came here to testify to what I witnessed with my naked eye and what I suffered on my own back, and I am not the only witness in the village to what happened. It was seen by about 500 inhabitants in the village. Therefore, this is a fact of life, namely, that the military and the police Serb forces undertook that operation against the inhabitants and against my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Can we go back into open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I appreciate your indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. Back into open session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Loku, you gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor on the 4th of June, 1999. That's a statement that you -- you signed and swore to. It was read back to you in your language and you were given a chance to make any corrections you wanted to make. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that I gave the statement. I made some corrections, but I don't know how the translator reflected my corrections in English, because I gave the statement in Albanian and it was translated by a translator in English. So it's -- it depends on him, how he has reflected in English what I did in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, at paragraph 3 of that statement you talk about some villages near Kotlina being shelled. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And those villages all had KLA members in them, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no knowledge that there were KLA members in those villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, you certainly know there were KLA members in the neighbouring village of Ivaja, don't you?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ivaja is a village near Kotline. Therefore, as I said in my testimony earlier, and it is correct and I will stand by this as long as I live because things are not easy to forget, on the 8th of March the Serbian forces launched an offensive against Ivaja.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You're really not answering my question and I don't want to stay here the whole day. All I asked you was: You know there were KLA members in the village of Ivaja, don't you? Because you told us that in your statement. You can just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave you the answer. No, I didn't know that there were -- that there were KLA members in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Hmm. In paragraph 3 of your statement, about halfway through, and this is in the -- this is -- this is in our evidence, Your Honours, as 4D15. Third paragraph on page 2. You said: "I knew that there were some UCK in the village of Ivaja, and I believe they were resisting Serb forces." Now, that's what you said, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not as if you are translating it to me in Albanian. I said that when Ivaja village was attacked some resistance was put up by the KLA, but not inside the village. The fighting took place in the outskirts of the village where the KLA resisted the Serb attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And that resistance resulted in a battle that lasted for three days between the KLA and the Serb forces, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. One day, not three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So when you said under oath to tell the truth like you are here in the Milosevic trial at page 2026: "During the resistance it lasted three days between the KLA and the Serb forces," speaking of the battle that was going on at Ivaja. So that wasn't true, when you testified to that in Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it was translated in this way, it is not true. I didn't declare that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So any time anything isn't what you want it to be, then the problem is the translators; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That's just an argument.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: In your statement to the OTP, in paragraph 15, you talk about some rockets that were being fired over your village. Actually, you talk about your village being shelled, and you said: "The shells seemed to be directed to land just outside the village in an effort to stop people from fleeing the village." Did you say that or is that another translation problem?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is approximately so. I said that the shells fell in the vicinity of the village, some tens of metres away from the houses. And my opinion was and is that they didn't want the population to leave the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, if the goal was to get the population to leave the village, why would they try to keep the population from leaving the village? Does that make any sense to you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think that's for later argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you think maybe they were trying to trap the KLA that were hiding in that village that later wound up killed? Do you think maybe that's why they were doing it that way?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, as you are putting it to me. The villagers didn't intend to leave the village. They didn't have any reason to leave. They were not afraid of anyone for anything. But when at the last moment the shelling started, they saw that they were trapped, and out of panic they wanted to find a way out of that situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, this tank that you claim was firing at your village, was it out in the open? Could you see it clearly?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tanks -- to put it more clearly, we couldn't see where the shelling was coming from. We saw only where they landed, in the vicinity of the village. But the sound of the shelling was from all sides of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I'm referring to your statement again, and this may be another translation error. Paragraph 16 you say: "While I was hiding at the top of the ravine, I saw a tank arrive at the top of the wooded hill to the south of the village, and this tank was machine-gunning over the village." Now, did you see a tank or not?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After the shelling, which lasted for half an hour or one hour, then I saw a tank entering the village. Not a single tank but several ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, this was the 24th of March, after NATO had started their campaign, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was the day of the 24th of March in the morning, and the massacre happened until the evening. As far as I know, NATO air-strikes started in the evening or at the night of the 24th of March. After that, genocide or the massacre was perpetrated against my people.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. I want to talk now just for a few moments with you about something else you told us. You've talked about a little bit this morning already. I'd like to read a paragraph to you from your statement and then ask you about it. You say: "Once they had completed the burning of the village and the execution of the men, the Serbs started to leave in the direction of Kacanik. One of their tanks broke down and it took some time before they could repair it. Once it had been repaired and all the Serbs had left the area, we came out of hiding and entered the village. We could hear livestock screaming where they were locked in buildings that were burning, and we all split up to go and release them." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So you claim to have been up hiding on the side of this hill and watched this horrible massacre, as you call it, in a hole on the side of a hill above the village, and as soon as you -- as soon as the Serbs leave you go rushing into the village and start saving livestock. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are putting it to me in this way. I was not the only one to return to the village. We were about 40 young people who returned, and we were all running in the direction of houses. Some of us were releasing the livestock, some were searching for dead bodies or injured persons. And in some houses we found three bodies. One of them was still alive. Two were already dead. So all of us were trying to do something to see if there was anything alive, not only livestock.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Loku, I can only ask you questions based upon what you told the Prosecutor and what's written in your statement. I have to rely on that as having some kind of accuracy, and what it says here that you said was: "We, we could hear livestock screaming where they were locked in buildings that were burning, and we all split up to go and release them." Now, is that wrong?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not wrong. We released livestock. We found the dead bodies. We found Zimer Loku who was still alive but seriously wounded. We found to the holes and saw them flattened out and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, no where do you say you went to the holes. In fact, you didn't go to the holes. You went and saved livestock and didn't go anywhere near those holes, did you?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally didn't go to the holes. There were others who went. I said I was not the only one who went back to the village. There were about 40 persons and each of them running to do something.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, you're the one that had seen what happened up in those holes. Why didn't you go up there to see if there was somebody up there you could help, somebody who was wounded, who was injured, that you could help instead of saving livestock?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were others who went to the holes. They, too, saw what happened. I was not the only one that witnessed the incident at the hole. The others had already gone there and seen that everything was finished there and that the earth was flattened out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown -- to have put up on the screen --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, is this a suitable time to interrupt?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, it would be, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, I think it would be. I -- Your Honour, I was looking at the answer the witness gave in closed session, and having regard to that answer which explained his earlier answer to my questions and explained his personal situation in respect to coming here and the absence of fear and absence of threats, I would suggest, I would apply that that record be made public. I don't think that the reasons suggested earlier for it to be private are extant anymore. So I respectfully ask that that be released to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no objection if the witness has no objection. I was only doing it to protect the witness, not to protect anything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We can do that without any difficulty, can we? Well, we're certainly satisfied that the whole session can be public and, therefore, steps will be taken to revoke the orders which were made for the private session and also for the earlier redaction. We will resume at 10 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Loku, I want you take a look at Exhibit P2296, which should be up here on the screen here momentarily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just carry on, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm trying to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, what is it you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: P2296. Well, that says it's P2296 but that's not what I had in mind. Maybe the Prosecution can help me. I'm looking for the -- oh, yeah, it is. It's the last page of that document. It has a drawing on it. If the usher could get us to the drawing that is located -- I suppose it's page 9 of that document maybe. There we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Can you see that on your screen, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If the witness's mic can be turned on. Thank up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Was there a building there in your village that you referred to as the ambulance building?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Where was that? Can you show us where that was?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'll show it to you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And just tell us if it already has some kind of a mark on it or something written by it.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have marked it with the short form AM standing for ambulance, just to show that that is the clinic building.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You just now drew a blue circle there, I guess; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll have that made a court exhibit, then, an in court exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for Judge Bonomy.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we'll make it an exhibit once you've finished using it, because in my experience is it causes problems as soon as you take the picture. Let's carry on with it on the screen as it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to go to a different exhibit and then come back to this, Judge, that's my problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you need the shot then. That's okay.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's IC35, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: 35? All right. Okay. Now I want to go to 4D14. And it's the second page of that document ending in the numbers 898.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. Sir, this is -- this is in English, and I don't think there's an Albanian version. At least I've not been advised that there was. It says that it is the interview of a person by the name of Hazbi Loku, a male, birth date 25 March 1961, from Kotlina. I take it that would be you?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what is written on this paper, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you recall giving an interview to the ICG or the OSCE, do you not?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave two or three statements in Skopje. I don't remember every organisation, but they dealt with crimes that were committed in Kotline.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Could we go back one page, please, to one that says 898 at the top right-hand corner. I don't know how we moved forward a page, but we did. Now, I know you can't read it, but that last full paragraph at the bottom of this, the interviewer says that you told him or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The witness has an Albanian version in front of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Oh, he does?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, if he does, that's good.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you have an Albanian version on the screen in front of you, sir? I'm told it's B/C/S, Your Honour. That last full paragraph reads as follows: "The group from the ambulance building was forced to walk to a well near the ambulance. They were all beaten up again and suffered serious injuries as a result of the torture. Although the victims were still alive, the perpetrators threw them into the well. Finally, the MUP threw hand-grenades into the well. The victims were torn to pieces. The dead bodies are still in the well." Is that the story you told just a few days after this happened, after you'd left your country, after you'd left Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not what I said. It has some elements but not in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I suspect and I suggest to you that that is what you said, and that after you talked to some people following the making of this statement you realised it was not correct and that it wasn't a well near the ambulance, but you were told that it was a hole up on the side of the hill. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document before me is in B/C/S, and I can see that there are many mistakes in it. I don't know now if these mistakes occurred during the translation or were done with a certain purpose in mind. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, after making that statement and apparently talking to some villagers you changed -- if what you said there was even close to true, you then changed your story, and you said that you had seen these people taken up a hill where there was a hole. You saw them beaten by men in police uniforms and bullet-proof vests that were blue camouflage in colour, also some soldiers in VJ uniforms, and that they were thrown into this hole, and then you later heard an explosion, and that you observed all this and saw all this happening. I suggest to you you didn't observe it. You really didn't see this happen, did you?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw everything that happened with my eyes and I felt it in my soul.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, if you saw everything that happened with your eyes, why did you describe it as a hole up on the side of this hill? You called it a hole, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: A hole or a well in my language has a same meaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So what you saw was a hole or a well up on the side of the hill; correct?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The two wells above the village, I knew that they were there because the villagers had tried to find water there. There are many wells in our village that provide villagers with water.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: But you didn't say a well or -- you didn't say two wells or two holes, you said a hole. You described one hole. And let's go back to that diagram. It's now -- I want to look at the one you made the marks on. That's IC31, is it? IC35. Let's look at that again. Now, that's attached to the end of this statement, so while you were giving this statement to the OTP where you talked about a hole up on the side of this hill, you drew this diagram, and on the diagram you drew one hole, didn't you, not two?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that you can see one hole in the photograph, but the holes were very close to each other, and I didn't find it reasonable to draw two holes. These are two separate holes which are -- which have only a couple of metres in between. That's why I didn't saw it necessary to represent two groups -- two holes there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... drew that map there, didn't you? One hole; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The witness has answered that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I want you to look at Exhibit P360 now. P360. And I suggest to you that you later learned that there were two holes up there and so you had to change your story again. So when you talked to the Prosecutor the other day, for the first time in your supplemental statement, and it would be at paragraph 2 of that statement, you wanted to change your prior statement and say: "I know there were two large holes," but you only learned that later. If you look at this picture that's on the screen now, these are pretty large holes, and they're pretty prominent, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The holes can be clearly seen on the photograph. They look large, but these photographs were taken when there was work going on there to recover the bodies. And this is what I meant earlier when I said when there is no vegetation you can see clearly what is in the picture, even though this photograph was taken from a distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So you still contend that you actually observed what happened there even though you changed the story about three times, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That's argumentative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It is entirely argumentative, and it's not advancing the matter, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: When you testified about this incident in the Milosevic case - I'm on page 2018 - Mr. Milosevic is asking you about this incident that happened in your village on the 24th, and you said this: "It was only after some days that we realised what had happened there, that we saw what had happened there." Now, that's the truth, isn't it? You didn't see what happened there that day. You learned what happened there days later. So you have no idea who it was that committed these acts, putting these people in these holes and so forth. You told the truth in Milosevic, I believe.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that in the way you are putting it to me. What happened, I saw it with my own eyes. That was said with a reference to something that was found later, two victims that were found later. This is what I meant, because at that time we didn't know who the victims were. We found about it later.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to move the admission of Exhibits 4D12, 13, 14, 15, and 16, which are all of this -- these witness's statements and accounts of these events. And with that I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We've had reference to 14 and 16, I think, and you also wish -- what are 12, 13 and 14 -- 12, 13 and 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: 12 and 13 are Milosevic transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Extracts from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No, the full transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. And -- and 15?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: 15 is his 18 May 1999 statement, that I think is also an OTP exhibit. 16 is the supplemental information sheet, and 14 is the ICG or OSCE.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The 18th of May statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's not the right date. It's the 4 June 1999 statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that's P2296.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We don't need it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No, we don't. We don't need it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, what is -- what is your position in relation to 4D12 and 13?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: These are the transcripts from Milosevic. It's -- it's the full transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I would ask to reserve that until the end of the testimony, because it just might well be that other parts of the transcript are put to him for clarification of those which have already been put to him. But normally the position is that only those extracts which have been asked about are the ones that are admissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that's a rule that I can understand before a jury, but here, we'll be here until kingdom come if we have to explore the whole testimony in real time in court that was given on two different occasions. Why can't we be left in due course to take account of the submissions that are made and compare the two in light of the challenges that have so far been made to the testimony? Yes, what's your position on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I do not object to the entire transcript going in if the Court feels it is necessary to provide some sort of context for the parts used. However, I -- I thought the Court might not want to be burdened by unnecessary paperwork, and the general practice has been that only those parts shown to be relevant in court would go in, those extracts used would go in, unless the whole thing is necessary to prove or establish the context in which something was said. Why I ask that it be reserved is that it might well be that some of the things from the Milosevic case that were put to him may well be better understood if other parts of the transcript are also put to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ackerman, what do you have to say about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I was -- as you correctly perceived, I was just trying to save a lot of time. I could very easily go through the parts that I've marked in this transcript that I want to bring to the Court's attention and introduce each page as opposed to the whole thing as I refer to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what's the estimate of your time for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: A couple of hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's consider the position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What -- what we will do is reserve the position on this for the moment. That will -- until we've heard all the evidence from the witness. That will not prejudice your position in any way, Mr. Ackerman, because at the very least we will allow you to submit the highlighted portions that you're referring to, and it may indeed be that that is the way forward, but we'll make a final decision on that once we've heard the re-examination. So meanwhile, we will deal with -- well, we don't need to deal positively with 14 and 16 because they're already part of the process. 15 is not necessary since it's a repetition of P2296. And we'll reserve our position on 12 and 13 pending the rest of this witness's evidence. And that takes us to Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Loku. I'm Branko Lukic. Together with my colleagues Mr. Ivetic and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Hold on, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just inquire. What's 3D -- or 4D15.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: 4D15 used or referred to at all?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no. Mr. Ackerman tells me it's a repetition of P2296 and, therefore, it won't be necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No. My information is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is it then?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: My information is P2296 is 4D -- is certainly not 4D -- well, there are -- there's 4D15, which I think is the OSCE statement. I'll just confirm that now. And there is another statement, which is 4D14, which was not referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I've been told that 4D16 is the supplemental information sheet that you submitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That 4D14 is the statement given to the OSCE.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
